title: Choose scaling actions and policy controls
summary: Distinguish size changes, instance-count changes and the settings that bound automatic adjustments. Actual timing, limits and billing depend on the service and hosting plan.

up.clue: A single instance needs a larger CPU/memory allocation. Name the increasing-size direction, not the scaling axis.

down.clue: One instance is resized to a smaller CPU/memory allocation after measurement shows spare capacity. Name the decreasing-size direction.

out.clue: A stateless tier grows from three same-sized workers to five. Name the increasing-count direction.

in.clue: After safely draining work, a pool removes redundant same-sized workers. Name the decreasing-count direction.

automatic.clue: Rules or schedules allocate and release capacity as demand changes, without an operator initiating each adjustment. Name this automated process.

cooldown.clue: In Azure Monitor, a rule must wait after a scale action before that same rule can become eligible again. Name the per-rule stabilization setting. Use the single-word duration-setting term.

minimum.clue: A profile’s lower permitted capacity boundary keeps baseline replicas available. Name this boundary setting, not its metric-failure fallback. Use a label ending in instance count.

maximum.clue: A profile’s upper permitted capacity boundary stops unbounded replica growth. Name this boundary setting. Use a label ending in instance count.
